scenes.heading: Adaptive immunity
scenes.sub: Why you usually only get chickenpox once
scenes.say: Once you've had chickenpox, you almost never catch it again. That lasting protection comes from the adaptive immune response, the third line of defence. It's slower to start, but it's specific, and it remembers.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A footy list where each player is trained for one opposition team
scenes.science: Millions of lymphocytes, each with one receptor shape, already exist
scenes.breaks: lymphocytes copy themselves by mitosis, and most on the 'list' are never picked at all.
scenes.say: Imagine a footy club with millions of players, each trained for one opposing team. When that team turns up, the coach picks the matching player. That's clonal selection. Then that player is copied into a whole team: clonal expansion. Some play now as effector cells, and some sit on the bench as memory cells.

scenes.heading: Getting started
scenes.say: A dendritic cell engulfs a pathogen and displays fragments on MHC class two. It travels to a lymph node, where only the matching helper T cell binds. That helper T cell is the captain. It releases cytokines that switch on both B cells and cytotoxic T cells.
scenes.caption: A dendritic cell engulfs a pathogen and displays fragments on MHC class II. It travels to a lymph node, where only the matching helper T cell binds. That helper T cell is the captain. It releases cytokines that switch on both B cells and cytotoxic T cells.

scenes.heading: Two branches

right.title: Cell-mediated
points: Bind infected cells on MHC I

scenes.say: The humoral response deals with pathogens in body fluids. Activated B cells become plasma cells that pump out antibodies. The cell-mediated response deals with cells that are already infected. Cytotoxic T cells spot them by their MHC class one display, then use perforin and granzymes to trigger apoptosis.

scenes.heading: What antibodies do
scenes.say: Antibodies are Y-shaped proteins with two binding sites. They don't destroy pathogens themselves. They neutralise them, clump them together, tag them for phagocytes, and activate complement.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: A rabbit gets antigen X on day 0, then X again plus new antigen Y on day 40. Compare the antibody responses.
lines: Memory is specific to each antigen
scenes.say: Antigen X on day zero gives a slow, low primary response. X again on day forty gives a fast, high secondary response, thanks to memory B cells. But new antigen Y gives only a primary response. Memory is specific.

points: Helper T cells activate both branches
scenes.say: Quick recap. Clonal selection picks the matching lymphocyte, which then multiplies. Helper T cells coordinate both branches. And the secondary response is faster, bigger and longer, because memory cells are already there. Now try the practice questions!
